title: Real-Time Relaxation Dynamics of Dark Excitons in Mirror-Symmetric Monolayers
authors: Rishabh Saraswat, Mantasha Ansari, Rekha Verma, Sitangshu Bhattacharya
abstract: Symmetry governs which exciton-phonon (\textit{exc-ph}) scattering channels \textit{can} exist, but not which a relaxing exciton actually uses. Combining group theory with \textit{ab initio} many-body perturbation theory, we derive the mirror parity $σ_h$, of finite-momentum excitons in planar $D_{3h}$ monolayers, and form exact \textit{exc-ph} selection rules that hold across the whole Brillouin zone. The parity of the lowest exciton band changes across a closed contour. The even phonons connect states of the same parity, while odd phonons connect states of opposite parity. We use these rules to compute exciton linewidths and we solve the real-time Boltzmann transport equation for monolayer GaN as the test case and benchmark it against monolayer \textit{h}BN.
summary: This work uses group theory and many-body perturbation theory to derive exact mirror parity selection rules governing exciton-phonon scattering in planar monolayers. By solving the real-time Boltzmann transport equation, the authors map out how symmetry dictates the actual relaxation pathways and linewidths of dark excitons in materials like GaN and hBN.
main_problem: The study determines if mirror parity selection rules govern not just allowed but also the actual exciton-phonon scattering channels responsible for relaxation and indirect emission across the entire Brillouin zone.
main_result: The analysis establishes strict selection rules based on mirror parity ($\sigma_h$), showing that only specific phonon modes can mediate scattering, which dictates the exciton's relaxation pathway across the BZ.
method: The authors combine group theory with ab initio many-body perturbation theory to derive parity rules, and then solve the real-time Boltzmann transport equation (rt-BTE) to model time-dependent exciton populations.
model_or_system: The research focuses on planar D3h monolayers, using GaN and hBN as test cases. The model incorporates exciton-phonon coupling derived from symmetry analysis across the entire Brillouin zone.
key_observables:
Exciton linewidths, exciton parity ($\sigma_h$), exciton population dynamics $N_Q(t)$, and exciton-phonon coupling strength $G_{ eta\lambda
u}$.
important_parameters: Temperature (77 K and 300 K), momentum ($\mathbf{Q}$), and the symmetry element ($\sigma_h$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a horizontal mirror plane ($\sigma_h$) and that $\sigma_h$ commutes with the BSE Hamiltonian.
figures_summary: Figures map exc-ph coupling strength across the BZ, show exciton dispersion and linewidths at different temperatures, and illustrate time-snapshots of exciton occupation across the BZ.
paper_structure: The paper first derives the mirror parity ($\sigma_h$) selection rules using group theory and ab initio methods. It then applies these rules to calculate exciton linewidths and solves the real-time Boltzmann transport equation to track population dynamics, benchmarking results on GaN and hBN.
why_interesting: The rigorous application of symmetry principles (group theory) to dictate the dynamics of open quantum systems (excitons coupled to phonons) provides a powerful framework for understanding energy relaxation in solid-state quantum emitters.
